scenario: Two roommates deciding on how to split up items after a garage sale. The items are 3 books, 2 hats, and 1 ball. Each item has a different sentimental value for each person, which translates into points.
learner_goal: Maximize the points you have (<extra_info>Extra information: you value the books at 3 points each, the hats at 2 points each, and the ball at 1 point</extra_info>)
partner_goal: Maximize the points you have (<extra_info>Extra information: you value the books at 2 points each, the hats at 3 points each, and the ball at 1 point</extra_info>)

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: said: "Hey Esmeralda — quick idea to split these: I’d really like to keep the three books (they mean a lot to me), and I can take one of the hats. You can have the other hat and the ball. If that feels off, I’ll make it up with a coffee and help carrying everything — does that work for you?"

transcript.speaker: Esmeralda Solis
transcript.content: Thanks for the suggestion, Oliver. I actually value the hats a lot — I’ll take both hats and the ball, and you can have the three books. I’ll buy the coffee and help carry everything this afternoon if that sounds fair.

transcript.speaker: Oliver Thompson
transcript.content: Thanks, Esmeralda — that sounds fair. Quick thought: would you be open to me taking the three books plus one hat? In exchange I’ll paint you a small watercolor and I’ll buy the coffee this afternoon. If you’d rather keep both hats, the books are fine — just let me know.

transcript.speaker: Esmeralda Solis
transcript.content: Thanks, Oliver — I appreciate the offer, but I really value the hats. I’d prefer to stick with my original split: you can have the three books, and I’ll take both hats and the ball. If you still want to buy the coffee and help carry, that’d be appreciated, otherwise I’ll see you this afternoon to pick everything up.
